intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to reach high-altitude runs and enjoy varied terrain suitable for all skill levels, with breathtaking panoramic views of 29 peaks over 4000m.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. A certified mountain guide leads you through untracked powder fields and challenging couloirs in the Mont Fort area, offering an adrenaline-packed adventure for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the Aletsch Glacier, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alpine peaks. A once-in-a-lifetime mountain experience combining culture and nature.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Enjoy locally sourced Gruyère and Emmental cheeses paired with Swiss wines and regional bread, immersing yourself in authentic Alpine culinary culture.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe. This full-day cross-country skiing experience takes you through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen lakes, with optional instruction from a local Nordic coach for beginners and intermediates.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked budget train or bus transfer toward Poschiavo. The Bernina Express or regional rail via Tirano connects to Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama, settle in, and rest after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a sandwich at the airport
meals.dinner: Pick up a quick snack or pre-packed meal at the airport convenience store before boarding your transfer (CHF 8–12). Arrive late so no restaurant dining tonight.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your train transfer in advance on SBB.ch for the best budget fares. The Poschiavo valley is remote — confirm your B&B host about late check-in arrangements. Pack light layers as temperatures in Poschiavo in February average -2°C to 4°C. Keep CHF cash on hand as some local spots may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Then take a short walk around the charming village of Poschiavo — explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Baroque Church of San Vittore, and the colorful Spaniol-style houses unique to this valley. This free self-guided stroll takes about 1.5–2 hours and gives you a feel for the local culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), just a short walk or free bus ride from the village center. In winter the lake may be partially frozen and the surrounding snow-covered landscape is stunning. Walk along the lakeside path (free) and take in the panoramic mountain views. Alternatively, rent cross-country ski equipment from a local rental shop in Poschiavo (approx. CHF 20–25/day) and try the beginner-friendly Nordic ski trails around the valley floor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village for a relaxed evening. Stroll through Poschiavo's old town as it lights up at dusk. Visit a local Grotto (traditional Ticino-style tavern) for a warm, affordable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee
meals.lunch: Grab a Panino or local pizza slice from a village bakery or café in Poschiavo (CHF 6–10)
meals.dinner: Grotto al Curt or a local Osteria in Poschiavo — try Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables, a regional specialty) for CHF 15–20

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits at 1,014m elevation. Dress in warm layers. The village is walkable and compact. Check the local tourist office (Turismo Valposchiavo) for free maps and any winter event listings. Cross-country ski rental shops may require a deposit.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Bernina Express (Rhaetian Railway) from Poschiavo station up toward Ospizio Bernina (2,253m) — one of the highest railway stations in the Alps. The train ride itself is a UNESCO World Heritage experience and a budget-friendly way to reach high alpine terrain (approx. CHF 12–18 one way with a Swiss Travel Pass or regional day pass). Enjoy breathtaking views of the Bernina massif, glaciers, and snow-covered peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Ospizio Bernina or Alp Grüm station. Alp Grüm offers a spectacular terrace viewpoint overlooking the Palü Glacier and the Poschiavo valley below. Enjoy snowshoeing or a winter hike on marked trails around the area (snowshoe rental approx. CHF 15–20 in Poschiavo before departure). The scenery is world-class and completely free once you're there.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo in the late afternoon. Warm up with a Vin Brulé (mulled wine) or hot chocolate at a local café. Spend the evening relaxing at the B&B or exploring the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich or buy one from the village bakery before boarding the train (CHF 5–8). There is a small restaurant at Alp Grüm but it is pricier — budget CHF 18–25 if dining there.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from the local Coop or Migros supermarket in Poschiavo (CHF 10–15 for pasta, sauce, and local cheese) — great budget option

day_by_day.notes: Check the Rhaetian Railway (rhb.ch) timetable in advance. A regional day pass or Swiss Half Fare Card can significantly reduce train costs. Ospizio Bernina can be extremely cold and windy — bring a windproof jacket, gloves, and a hat. Snowshoe trails are marked but always check avalanche bulletins at slf.ch before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to skiing! Take the Bernina Express or a regional bus to Livigno, Italy (approx. 45–60 min from Poschiavo via the Forcola di Livigno pass road — check winter road conditions). Livigno is a duty-free ski resort just across the Italian border offering some of the most affordable ski passes in the Alps. Purchase a day ski pass (approx. €35–45, significantly cheaper than Swiss resorts). Rent ski equipment at one of Livigno's many budget rental shops (approx. €20–30/day for skis, boots, and poles).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing in Livigno's 115km of pistes. The resort suits all levels — beginners can enjoy the gentle Mottolino and Carosello 3000 sectors while intermediate skiers can explore longer red runs with stunning views of the surrounding peaks. Take a lunch break on the mountain.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up at the B&B. Enjoy a quiet evening in the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat well before a full day of skiing
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant in Livigno — pasta or pizza on the slopes (€10–15). Alternatively, pack your own lunch to save money.
meals.dinner: Local Osteria in Poschiavo — try Polenta with local cheese or Brasato (braised beef) for CHF 16–22

day_by_day.notes: Verify the Forcola di Livigno road is open in winter — it sometimes closes due to snow. Alternatively, take a taxi or shared shuttle from Poschiavo (ask your B&B host for recommendations). Livigno is duty-free so fuel, alcohol, and tobacco are cheaper there. Bring your passport as you are crossing into Italy. Book ski rentals online in advance for discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Valposchiavo (Poschiavo Valley) on a self-guided winter walk or e-bike ride (e-bike rental approx. CHF 25–35/day from local providers). Head south along the valley toward Brusio, famous for the UNESCO-listed Brusio Circular Viaduct — a stunning spiral railway bridge used by the Bernina Express. The walk from Poschiavo to Brusio takes about 1.5–2 hours through snow-dusted chestnut forests and traditional stone villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Brusio Circular Viaduct up close and watch the Bernina Express spiral through it — a truly unique sight. Explore the small village of Brusio and its historic stone architecture. Return to Poschiavo by regional bus (CHF 3–5) or walk back along the valley trail. In the afternoon, visit the Museo di Poschiavo (local history museum, approx. CHF 5 entry) to learn about the valley's unique cultural blend of Swiss-German, Italian, and Romansh influences.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner tonight at one of Poschiavo's better-regarded restaurants as a mid-trip reward, while still keeping costs reasonable.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch with local bread, cheese (Formaggio d'alpe), and cured meats from the Poschiavo market or Coop (CHF 8–12) — eat near the viaduct for a memorable setting
meals.dinner: Ristorante Croce Federale or similar in Poschiavo — try Risotto with local mushrooms or Capretto (roasted kid goat) for CHF 20–28

day_by_day.notes: The Brusio Viaduct is one of the most photographed railway structures in Switzerland — bring your camera. Check the Bernina Express timetable to time your visit to the viaduct when a train passes through (roughly every 2 hours). The valley walk is mostly flat and suitable for all fitness levels even in winter with proper footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express north from Poschiavo to St. Moritz (approx. 45 min, CHF 15–22 one way). St. Moritz is one of the world's most famous ski resorts but you can enjoy it on a budget by focusing on free activities. Walk around the frozen Lake St. Moritz (free), admire the glamorous village atmosphere, and enjoy the stunning Engadin valley panoramas. Visit the Segantini Museum exterior or the free lakeside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: For a budget ski experience in the St. Moritz area, head to Corviglia ski area and purchase a half-day afternoon ski pass (approx. CHF 45–55 — pricier than Livigno but worth it for the iconic experience). Alternatively, skip skiing and try the free public sledding run at Muottas Muragl (cable car approx. CHF 20 return) or simply snowshoe on marked free trails around the lake. Return to Poschiavo by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Poschiavo, enjoy a final relaxed evening in the village. Visit the local Grotto for a farewell drink with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — pack a snack for the train
meals.lunch: In St. Moritz, avoid the expensive resort restaurants. Instead, grab a Wurst (sausage) from a street stand or a sandwich from the Coop supermarket in the village (CHF 8–12)
meals.dinner: Back in Poschiavo — budget-friendly Pizzeria or Trattoria, pizza or pasta for CHF 14–18

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is notoriously expensive — stick to free sightseeing and avoid sit-down restaurants there. The Bernina Express between Poschiavo and St. Moritz is itself a highlight — sit on the right side of the train heading north for the best glacier views. Saturday can be busy on the slopes so arrive early if skiing.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the B&B. Take a last peaceful morning walk through Poschiavo village, revisit your favorite spots, and pick up local souvenirs — try the Coop or local shops for affordable Swiss chocolate, local honey, or Valposchiavo herbal teas (CHF 5–15). Pack your bags and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, take the Bernina Express or regional train toward Tirano (Italy) or Chur (Switzerland) to connect to your onward journey to the airport. The Tirano–Milan train connection reaches Milan in about 2.5 hours, connecting to Malpensa or Linate airports. The Chur–Zurich connection takes about 1.5 hours to Zurich Airport. Enjoy the final alpine scenery on your train journey out of the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Switzerland. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, mountain scenery, and authentic Swiss-Italian alpine culture — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final included breakfast at B&B — enjoy it fully!
meals.lunch: Pack leftovers or grab a final Panino from the village bakery for the train journey (CHF 5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane — budget CHF 15–25 if eating at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your train connections on SBB.ch the night before departure. Allow extra time for connections as mountain trains can run on tight schedules. The Bernina line can experience delays in heavy snowfall — have a buffer of at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Leave a review for your B&B host and the local tourism board to support this small community.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle into your room and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama in Poschiavo (~22:30–23:30 depending on transfer). Check in, unpack, and get a good night's sleep to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit / airport dining
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport or convenience store en route to Poschiavo. Consider packing a sandwich or grabbing a quick bite at Zurich/Milan airport before your transfer.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is located in the Graubünden canton near the Italian border. Depending on your arrival airport (Zurich ~3h drive, or Milan Malpensa ~2h drive), arrange a pre-booked taxi or rental car. Roads may be icy — confirm winter tires. No activities planned tonight; rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast at the Berninapass Panorama, taking in the stunning alpine views over Poschiavo valley. After breakfast, explore the charming historic village of Poschiavo on foot — stroll through the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate architecture and visit the main square Piazza Comunale.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45 min drive via the Forcola di Livigno pass — check road conditions). Livigno offers excellent beginner-to-intermediate slopes and is a great warm-up day for the week. Rent ski equipment locally if needed and enjoy a half-day on the pistes. Alternatively, explore the Bernina Pass area on snowshoes if road conditions are challenging.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by late afternoon. Relax at the B&B and freshen up. Head into the village for a leisurely dinner at a local Graubünden restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — expect fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the Livigno slopes — try a hearty plate of pasta or a local soup (budget CHF 20–35).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse or a local trattoria in Poschiavo — try pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables), a regional Graubünden specialty (budget CHF 30–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Livigno is technically in Italy but easily accessible from Poschiavo. Bring your passport. Livigno is a duty-free zone, making ski equipment rental and après-ski drinks more affordable. Check Forcola di Livigno pass opening status in winter — it may require chains or be closed; confirm the day before.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take the iconic Bernina Express train (or drive) from Poschiavo to St. Moritz (approx. 1 hour by train — one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world, a UNESCO World Heritage route). Arrive in St. Moritz and head to the Corviglia ski area via the funicular from the town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon skiing the world-famous Corviglia slopes above St. Moritz. With 350km of runs in the Engadin ski region, there's terrain for all levels. Enjoy the glamorous mountain atmosphere and well-groomed pistes. Take the cable car up to Piz Nair (3,057m) for panoramic views of the Engadin valley.
day_by_day.evening: Explore St. Moritz village before catching the return train to Poschiavo. Browse the upscale shops or enjoy a warm drink at a café. Return to Poschiavo by early evening.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mountain restaurant on Corviglia — try rösti with cheese or a warming goulash soup. Mid-range options available (CHF 25–40).
meals.dinner: Back in Poschiavo, enjoy dinner at Albergo Ristorante Croce Federale — a cozy local spot serving traditional Swiss-Italian cuisine (CHF 30–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a highlight in itself — book tickets in advance via SBB (Swiss Federal Railways). A day ski pass for Corviglia/St. Moritz costs approximately CHF 75–85. Consider a combo rail+ski pass for savings. St. Moritz is upscale — stick to mid-mountain restaurants for better value.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from Poschiavo for the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour. Drive or take trains via Chur and Interlaken to Grindelwald/Lauterbrunnen (approx. 3–3.5 hours total travel). Board the cogwheel train from Grindelwald Terminal up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jungfraujoch: visit the Ice Palace (carved entirely in glacial ice), walk on the Aletsch Glacier (the longest glacier in the Alps), enjoy the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform with breathtaking 360° views of the Bernese Alps, and browse the Top of Europe exhibition. This is a once-in-a-lifetime alpine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back to Grindelwald or Interlaken by late afternoon. Enjoy dinner in Interlaken before the return journey to Poschiavo (consider an overnight stay in Interlaken if the return drive feels too long — budget hotels available for CHF 80–120).

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure — request an early breakfast from your hosts the night before.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — a unique dining experience at 3,454m. Expect Swiss classics like fondue or hot soup (CHF 30–50). Alternatively, bring packed snacks to save costs.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Interlaken at Restaurant Schuh or a local Swiss restaurant — try Bernese-style dishes like Berner Platte (assorted meats and sauerkraut) (CHF 30–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch tickets cost approximately CHF 145–165 per person (book online in advance for discounts via jungfrau.ch). Altitude sickness is possible at 3,454m — ascend slowly and stay hydrated. Dress in warm layers; temperatures at the top can be -15°C or colder. This is a long travel day — consider whether an overnight in Interlaken makes more sense logistically.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Poschiavo if you stayed overnight in Interlaken, or rest and recover at the B&B after yesterday's big day. After breakfast, prepare for the Zermatt Ski Safari. Drive from Poschiavo toward Zermatt (approx. 2.5–3 hours via Chur and Visp). Park at Täsch (cars are not allowed in Zermatt) and take the shuttle train into the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari — explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Ski across multiple sectors: Rothorn, Gornergrat, and Klein Matterhorn (the highest ski area in the Alps at 3,883m). The views of the Matterhorn from the slopes are absolutely iconic.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy après-ski in Zermatt village — the car-free village is magical in the evening with horse-drawn carriages and glowing chalets. Explore the village, visit the Matterhorn Museum, and enjoy dinner before returning to Poschiavo (or consider a one-night stay in Zermatt for the full experience).

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama (or hotel breakfast in Interlaken if returning).
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at one of Zermatt's mid-mountain restaurants — try Chez Vrony or Findlerhof for stunning Matterhorn views and Swiss cuisine (CHF 30–50). Book ahead as these are popular.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt at Restaurant Whymper-Stube — a cozy, mid-range spot named after the first Matterhorn climber, serving Swiss fondue and raclette (CHF 35–55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt day ski pass costs approximately CHF 85–95. The Zermatt Ski Safari experience (guided) may have an additional cost — book in advance through zermatt.ch. Parking at Täsch costs approximately CHF 15/day. Zermatt is one of Switzerland's most popular ski resorts — book any restaurants in advance. The Klein Matterhorn cable car reaches 3,883m; dress extremely warmly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Poschiavo from Zermatt (if you stayed overnight) or enjoy a relaxed morning at the B&B. After breakfast, head to Davos for the Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail experience (approx. 2 hours drive from Poschiavo via Chur). Davos is the highest city in Europe and home to 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Glide through the stunning Davos-Klosters landscape on the Nordic trails — the Davos Flüela and Sertig valley trails are particularly scenic. Cross-country skiing is a wonderful contrast to downhill skiing and offers a full-body workout through pristine alpine scenery. Equipment rental is available in Davos town center.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-deserved Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening in Davos — warm up after a day on the Nordic trails with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. This is the perfect way to celebrate your penultimate evening in the Alps. Return to Poschiavo afterward.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a quick stop at a Nordic trail hut/café in Davos — try a warming Landjäger (Swiss dried sausage) with bread and hot chocolate (CHF 15–25).
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at Bergrestaurant Schatzalp or Restaurant Bolgenschanze in Davos — traditional cheese fondue with crusty bread, cornichons, and pearl onions, paired with Swiss white wine or hot tea (CHF 40–60 per person including drinks).

day_by_day.notes: Nordic trail pass in Davos costs approximately CHF 15–20. Cross-country ski rental is approximately CHF 25–35. Davos is about 2 hours from Poschiavo — an early start is recommended. The fondue evening experience is best booked in advance, especially on weekends. Davos also has excellent downhill skiing at Parsenn and Jakobshorn if you prefer to mix activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama, savoring the panoramic mountain views. Take a gentle farewell walk around Poschiavo village — visit the historic church of San Vittore, stroll along the lake (Lago di Poschiavo), and pick up local souvenirs such as Graubünden nut cake (Nusstorte) or local cheeses from a village shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of the B&B. Depending on your departure flight, begin your transfer to the airport (Zurich ~3h, Milan Malpensa ~2h). If time allows, make a scenic stop at the Bernina Pass viewpoint for final alpine photos — the Lago Bianco (White Lake) at the pass is stunning in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland with incredible memories of the Swiss Alps. Airport transfer and departure.

meals.breakfast: Final full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Poschiavo before departure — try the local bakery or Café/Bar in the village square for a sandwich and coffee (CHF 15–20). Alternatively, pack snacks for the road.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich or Milan Malpensa, or an in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your checkout time with the B&B hosts. If flying from Zurich, allow at least 3.5 hours for the drive plus check-in time. The Bernina Pass road (in the direction of St. Moritz) is one of the most scenic drives in Switzerland — a beautiful final memory. Consider purchasing a Nusstorte (Engadin nut tart) as a souvenir — they travel well. Safe travels!

day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.

meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Light in-room welcome board arranged by the B&B — local cured meats, Graubünden dried beef (Bündnerfleisch), artisan cheeses, and Poschiavo valley bread with a bottle of regional Pinot Noir.

The drive from Zurich is approximately 2.5 hours; from Milan Malpensa approximately 2 hours. Confirm late check-in with the B&B in advance. Pack ski gear or arrange rental for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B with panoramic Alpine views. After breakfast, explore the charming historic village of Poschiavo on foot — stroll through the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate mansions, visit the Collegiate Church of San Vittore, and soak in the serene winter atmosphere of this UNESCO-recognized cultural landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Diavolezza ski area (approx. 30–40 min drive via the Bernina Pass road), one of the most spectacular glacier ski areas in the Alps. Enjoy afternoon skiing on the Diavolezza glacier with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Hire a private ski guide for a personalized introduction to the terrain. Rent premium ski equipment on-site if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a refined dinner at Ristorante Suisse or Albergo Croce Federale — both offer elevated regional cuisine. Enjoy Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with local cheese and vegetables), slow-braised venison, and a curated selection of Graubünden wines.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass — fresh bread, local jams, Bündnerfleisch, soft-boiled eggs, yogurt with mountain honey, and freshly brewed coffee with panoramic valley views.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Diavolezza summit restaurant — enjoy hearty Rösti, Alpine soup, and hot chocolate at 2,978m elevation with jaw-dropping glacier panoramas.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse, Poschiavo — regional Graubünden cuisine featuring Pizzoccheri, braised venison with polenta, and a bottle of Malanser Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza is accessible via the Bernina Express road or by taking the Rhaetian Railway to Pontresina and then the Diavolezza cable car. A private car or taxi is recommended for flexibility. Check snow and weather conditions before heading up. Lift passes can be purchased on-site or online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Board the iconic Bernina Express (Rhaetian Railway) from Poschiavo station for a scenic morning journey through the UNESCO World Heritage Bernina line — crossing dramatic viaducts, glaciers, and snow-covered Alpine passes. Arrive in St. Moritz (approx. 45 min) — the crown jewel of luxury Alpine resorts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Zermatt Ski Safari Experience (adapted to Corviglia/St. Moritz ski area for the day): Engage a private ski instructor and explore the world-class Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz — 350km of immaculate pistes, stunning Engadine valley views, and perfectly groomed runs for all levels. Enjoy the legendary St. Moritz ski culture with access to exclusive mountain clubs.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in St. Moritz — Chesa Veglia (a 17th-century farmhouse restaurant) is the quintessential luxury choice, offering traditional cheese fondue, raclette, and fine Swiss wines in an intimate, candlelit setting. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cold cuts, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Paradiso mountain restaurant on Corviglia — a legendary St. Moritz institution with panoramic Engadine views, serving truffle pasta, grilled meats, and premium wines.
meals.dinner: Chesa Veglia, St. Moritz — traditional Swiss cheese fondue and raclette in a historic 17th-century farmhouse setting. Reserve well in advance. Pair with a Fendant du Valais white wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a world-class scenic journey — book first-class panoramic seats in advance through the Rhaetian Railway website. Return to Poschiavo via private luxury transfer in the evening (approx. 45 min). St. Moritz lift passes can be purchased at the Corviglia cable car base station.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour: Depart early by private transfer to Grindelwald or Interlaken (approx. 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo). Board the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and the eternal snow plateau with awe-inspiring views of the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending from Jungfraujoch, enjoy a premium afternoon skiing session at Grindelwald First ski area — a spectacular high-altitude ski domain with views of the Eiger North Face. Hire a private guide for a curated run selection across the First and Männlichen areas.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Grindelwald before the return transfer to Poschiavo. The Michelin-recognized Restaurant Firestarter at Hotel Belvedere or the elegant dining room at Grand Hotel Regina offer exceptional Alpine cuisine. Return to Poschiavo by private luxury transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure — light and energizing with fresh bread, eggs, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Crystal Restaurant at 3,454m — a truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience above the clouds. Enjoy warm Alpine soups, pasta, and hot beverages.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter, Hotel Belvedere, Grindelwald — contemporary Alpine cuisine with premium ingredients, featuring dishes like Bernese lamb, truffle risotto, and a curated Swiss wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch tickets must be booked well in advance — purchase the 'Good Morning Ticket' for early access and lower pricing. The round trip from Grindelwald takes approximately 3–4 hours including exploration time. Dress in very warm layers as temperatures at 3,454m can be extreme. Altitude sickness is possible — take it slowly upon arrival at the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Freeride Experience: Depart by private transfer to Verbier (approx. 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo). Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier — one of the world's top freeride destinations and home of the legendary Freeride World Tour. A certified IFMGA mountain guide will lead you through Verbier's iconic off-piste terrain including the Vallon d'Arby and Mont Gelé couloirs (terrain matched to your skill level).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Verbier's 410km of ski terrain with your private guide. Access the Mont Fort glacier at 3,330m for high-altitude powder runs and panoramic views across four countries. Enjoy the vibrant après-ski culture at Verbier's legendary mountain bars.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at the iconic Farm Club or Pub Mont Fort in Verbier — the heartbeat of Verbier's luxury social scene. Dinner at Restaurant La Grange au Feu or the Michelin-starred Rosalp for an exceptional fine dining experience before the return transfer to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before early departure — hearty and warming with eggs, local cheeses, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cabane du Mont Fort (3,330m) — a legendary high-altitude mountain hut serving hearty Alpine fare including Croûte au fromage, soups, and warming Glühwein with extraordinary panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Restaurant La Grange au Feu, Verbier — rustic luxury Alpine dining featuring Valais beef fondue, raclette with local Valais cheeses, and an extensive Swiss and French wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Verbier freeride terrain is for intermediate to advanced skiers. Inform your guide of your exact skill level in advance so the experience is tailored appropriately. Avalanche safety equipment (beacon, probe, shovel) is provided by the guide. Book the IFMGA guide through Verbier's Bureau des Guides at least 2 weeks in advance. Return transfer to Poschiavo is approximately 2.5–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail Experience: Depart by private transfer to Davos (approx. 1.5 hours from Poschiavo). Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos — the highest city in Europe at 1,560m. Hire a private Nordic ski instructor for a guided tour through the stunning Flüela and Dischma valleys, passing frozen lakes and pristine snow-covered forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Nordic morning, transition to downhill skiing at Parsenn — one of Switzerland's largest and most prestigious ski areas, shared between Davos and Klosters. Enjoy the legendary Weissfluhjoch runs and the famous 12km Parsenn Derby descent with a private ski guide.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Davos's finest restaurants — Bündnerstube at Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère offers exceptional Graubünden regional cuisine in an elegant Belle Époque setting. Enjoy Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle), Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), and premium Graubünden wines before the return transfer to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure — full Alpine spread with fresh bread, local honey, Bündnerfleisch, cheeses, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Weissfluhjoch (2,844m) on the Parsenn — panoramic mountain restaurant serving Rösti, Alpine soups, and warm beverages with sweeping views over Davos and the Graubünden Alps.
meals.dinner: Bündnerstube, Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère, Davos — elegant regional Graubünden cuisine in a historic grand hotel setting. Pair with a bottle of Malanser Completer or Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski equipment rental is available at the Davos Nordic Center near the Flüela trailhead. Classic and skate skiing styles are both available — specify your preference when booking the instructor. The Parsenn ski area lift pass is separate from the Nordic trails. A combined day pass covering both is available at the Davos tourist office.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely, indulgent breakfast at the B&B with panoramic views of the Bernina massif. Take a peaceful morning walk through the snow-covered streets of Poschiavo's historic center, visiting the weekly Sunday market if available. Browse local artisan shops for Graubünden specialties — Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart), local wines, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last afternoon ski session at Diavolezza glacier (30–40 min from Poschiavo) — a perfect farewell to the Swiss Alps with one final run on the glacier beneath Piz Bernina. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxing spa afternoon at a nearby luxury wellness facility in Pontresina or St. Moritz (Kempinski Grand Hotel des Bains offers exceptional spa facilities).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant in Poschiavo or a short drive to Pontresina — Ristorante Albergo Croce Federale in Poschiavo or the elegant dining room at Hotel Saratz in Pontresina. Celebrate an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps with a premium tasting menu and a bottle of vintage Graubünden Pinot Noir. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury farewell breakfast at B&B Berninapass — full spread with fresh pastries, local cheeses, Bündnerfleisch, smoked salmon, eggs, fresh fruit, yogurt with mountain honey, and a celebratory glass of Prosecco.
meals.lunch: Light mountain lunch at Diavolezza summit restaurant or a picnic-style lunch prepared by the B&B with local specialties to enjoy on the slopes.
meals.dinner: Hotel Saratz, Pontresina — elegant fine dining featuring a seasonal tasting menu with Engadine and Graubünden ingredients, paired with a curated wine flight. A perfect luxury farewell to the Swiss Alps.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the B&B and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon activities. Book the farewell dinner reservation at Hotel Saratz well in advance as it is popular on weekends. Arrange the departure transfer in advance — whether returning to Zurich Airport, Milan Malpensa, or another hub. The Bernina Express also offers a scenic departure option back toward Chur or St. Moritz for onward connections.
